# Orchestrate a multi-step process: Airtable

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers process-orchestration work end to end across Airtable, Slack and Telegram.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Stamp & Shape Job
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Route by Work Type
6. Process 'sync' → Airtable
7. Fast-Track 'async' + Alert
8. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
9. Merge Routed Work
10. Align Field Names
11. Tag Pipeline Metadata
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
15. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing process-orchestration work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Stamp & Shape Job → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Route by Work Type → Process 'sync' → Airtable → Fast-Track 'async' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Slack aligned by hand for process orchestration
- Process orchestration work where "Stamp & Shape Job" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Process orchestration work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Slack in step for process orchestration, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Airtable or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this process-orchestration build
- Branches rejoin before Airtable, so a process-orchestration run reports once rather than 17 times
- Every process-orchestration run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Airtable
- Fans the same result out to Telegram in the same run, for process orchestration

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your process orchestration process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole process-orchestration payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
